history_findings: Weight loss, decreased appetite, and low-grade fever
History of cigarette smoking and alcohol use
Vocal overuse from teaching for 20 years

additional_considerations.rationale: Can cause hoarseness, loss of appetite and fatigue, but does not fit the weight loss or lymphadenopathy.
Left atrial enlargement can compress the recurrent laryngeal nerve; more common in women with prior rheumatic fever, with palpitations, easy fatigue, a diastolic murmur and tachycardia.
Long-standing reflux can irritate and inflame the vocal cords; symptoms are typically linked to meals and lying down.

source_issues: e008: 'Deep Tendon Reflexes (DTRs) 4+ symmetric' is implausible (hyperreflexia with clonus) next to an otherwise unremarkable exam and may be an OCR error for 2+; kept as written with a flag (x016). The line is also filed under Extremities.
e007: 'Bowel sounds x 4 quadrants' has no sign; read as present with a flag (x013).
e002: 'low-grade fever' is given without a value; the doorway temperature is 99.9°F.
Note SH 'CAGE (014)' is an OCR artifact for 0/4.
Note SH says three glasses of wine a day 'for 30 years'; the script gives no drinking duration (added to f037 with a flag).
Note FH says the mother had 'hypothyroidism'; the patient says 'thyroid disease'. The patient's wording was kept.
Note HPI quotes the patient as saying 'I have had a mild fever'; in the script he only feels hot and did not measure his temperature.
p007 asks about recent changes in voice use; the answer (teacher for 20 years, now retired) does not address it directly. The note and gold #3 read it as voice overuse.
p009 asks about sore throat, runny nose and cough; the answer gives only 'the flu 4 weeks ago' (cough is denied later in p021).
p016 asks about swelling or bumps in the head or neck; the answer describes a sensation of a lump in the throat, not a palpable mass. The exam finds right anterior cervical lymphadenopathy.
Gold #2 lists 'GERD' as a history finding; the patient reports constant heartburn but no GERD diagnosis.
Gold #1 lists both 'Cervical lymphadenopathy' and 'Right cervical lymphadenopathy' (duplicate). Gold #2 'Temperature 99. 9°F' has a stray space (cleaned).
The challenging question has a doubled opening quotation mark ('""Will I regain my voice?"').
The raw sheet's 'Closure' section contains unrelated text (exam duration, topics 'math, science, and history'); the sample closure calls the patient 'Mr. Jefferson' instead of Oliver Jackson.
p008 topic says 'Exposure to cold water or dust' while the question asks about time in the cold.
e006 (Heart) gives the rhythm but not the rate, and mentions murmurs and rubs but not gallops.

The hoarse, slow speech from the SP notes is added as an observable sp_notes exam record (x017).
